rule: Burn-in is taken from the OLDEST side of the series only.
rationale: The newest observations are the most valuable validation evidence and must never be consumed as warm-up.
enforcement_point: Origin selection: first origin = min_date + 64 days.

rule: The latest origin is FORCED at max_date - 30 whenever it qualifies.
rationale: Guarantees the newest observations are the last thing predicted rather than the first thing lost. This is what lifted newest-preservation from 68 to 90 of 90 series.
enforcement_point: Origin selection: append max_date - 30 to the sampled origin list.

rule: A valid origin requires at least 20 REAL OBSERVED target dates inside the 30-day horizon.
rationale: Replaces the strict 'exactly 30 contiguous days' rule, which discarded late origins on gappy series and left all 20 IOPS series with no backtest after December 2022.
enforcement_point: Origin validity test, alongside the 65-row minimum training requirement.

rule: Do NOT fill, resample, interpolate or invent dates.
rationale: Sparse windows are handled by accepting fewer real targets, never by manufacturing observations. P4 refused to fill dates and P5 must not either.
enforcement_point: No resampling step exists anywhere in the P5 pipeline.

rationale: Prevents a visual offset between the actual line and the model estimate.
enforcement_point: Row-level assertion before every checkpoint write.

rule: actual_value MUST come from actuals_normalized for that same (series_id, target_date).
rationale: The actual is joined, never recomputed or carried from the model's own training frame.
enforcement_point: Post-batch join assertion against actuals_normalized with an exact-match requirement.

rule: train_end_date MUST be strictly less than target_date.
rationale: Prevents leakage of future actuals into training.
enforcement_point: Row-level assertion before every checkpoint write.

rule: Minimum training rows per origin remains 65 (LAGS + HORIZON + 5).
rationale: Unchanged from the HDD reference implementation, so P5 output stays comparable.
